summary: Pier light on Lake Erie since 1835; the present Art Deco steel tower was commissioned in 1936 and automated in 1972.

access.note: The US Lighthouse Society archive lists the station as not open to the public; the light is a Coast Guard aid.

events.note: First Huron Harbor light on the west pier
Wooden tower destroyed by a storm in May
Iron tower with fourth-order lens (LighthouseFriends: built three years after 1854)
Iron beacon moved about 120 ft NE near new end of west pier, June
Rear range light in operation 29 August (LighthouseFriends)
Steel Art Deco tower commissioned 8 April
Lantern room removed and 375 mm lens installed

notes_for_editor: NRHP nomination text is not digitised (22 KB placeholder). Much of the narrative rests on LighthouseFriends (copyrighted; paraphrased, one short quote). Platt 1838 and Sandusky Daily Register 1890 are second-hand via LighthouseFriends. Wikipedia/OSM give 1939 for the present tower; omitted from the story as it has no primary source. Keeper roster is from the USLHS archive and was not confirmed in primary registers; the Siggens and Irby discrepancies are noted. Newspaper search at Chronicling America found nothing for Huron. Bulletin 1919 lights established entry is not clearly the range light.
